funding: UNVERIFIED on institutional pages. The programme page advertises no scholarship. Austria's national route for a Tunisian would be an OeAD/Ernst Mach-type grant applied for separately and much earlier than admission — not verified here, so no amount or deadline is asserted.

verdictWhy: This is the single best structural fit in this slice: an English-taught MA that only asks for 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree', has no live audition, no German, and is explicitly aimed at people building instruments at the Design/Technology–Composition boundary — which is what a software engineer with a synth habit actually is. institution: Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, Faculty of Art and Design
stillExists2027: YES — active, no discontinuation notice. Annual winter-semester intake with a fixed 31 March deadline, so a 2027 entry is on the published pattern.
award: Master of Fine Arts (M.F.A.) — a real second-cycle degree from a state university. Not a certificate.
acceptsQuote: Entry is on 'a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Media Art and Design' OR 'a first university degree recognized as professionally relevant by the responsible examination committee.' That second clause is the door for a software-engineering BSc, but it is a committee judgement, not an entitlement — and the committee decides on the artistic portfolio.
liveAudition: NO LIVE AUDITION, and normally no interview either. Quote: 'Applicants must also pass an aptitude test based on their artistic portfolio' and 'A personal interview is usually not a compulsory part of the procedure.' The aptitude test IS a portfolio review — decided on documents.
portfolioSpec: 'Artistic portfolio, i.e. a compilation of own artistic/creative works (formats: PDF (max. 20 MB); if applicable, links to hosted interactive or time-based works)'. No minimum number of works and no duration cap published. Deadline = 31 March, uploaded via Bauhaus.CampusPortal.
costForTunisian: No tuition fee. Quote: 'No, there are no tuition fees, however enrolled students must pay a semester contribution fee'. The exact semester contribution amount is not stated on this page — UNVERIFIED (Thuringian semester contributions typically sit in the EUR 250–300/semester range but I will not assert a figure the university did not publish).
funding: UNVERIFIED — no programme-level scholarship is advertised on this page. DAAD is the realistic route for a Tunisian and is a separate, much earlier application, but nothing on the Weimar page substantiates an amount or deadline.
applicationDeadline: 'Please complete your application by uploading all necessary documents by 31 March' — recurring annual deadline, PRIOR CYCLE confirmed, expected to hold for 31 March 2027.
languageOfInstruction: English-language curriculum with some German-taught modules. REQUIRES BOTH: 'German language proficiency: A2 level minimum' AND 'English language proficiency: C1 level (e.g. TOEFL min. 95 or IELTS min. 7.0)'.
correction: INPUT UNDERSTATED THE GATE. This is not just 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — it demands German A2 AND English C1 at IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 95, which is a high English bar (most programmes in this slice ask 6.0–6.5). Also, the interview the input implies is 'usually not a compulsory part of the procedure' — the real gate is a pure portfolio aptitude test.
verdictWhy: Structurally friendly — no audition, no interview, decided purely on portfolio, no tuition — but two hard prerequisites he does not have: German A2 and IELTS 7.0 (not 6.0). Both are achievable by March 2027 if he starts German now, and the deadline gives him time. Also be clear this is a media-art MFA, not an electronic-music degree: he would be admitted as an artist working in media, not as a producer.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
stillExists2027: YES — active. Entrance examination dates are published annually; most recent published window '27 April 2026 to 28 April 2026'. A 2027 equivalent is on the same pattern (PRIOR CYCLE).
award: Master of Arts (M.A.), two-year programme at a state Hochschule. Real second-cycle degree.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE — but effectively gated by the exam, not the degree
acceptsQuote: The published requirement is artistic, not disciplinary: applicants must submit 'at least three representative works which demonstrate the ability to artistically incorporate the use of digital media, especially in the field of computer music.' No music degree is named as compulsory — but the entrance examination assumes conservatoire-level computer-music knowledge.
liveAudition: NOT an instrumental audition, but something worse for this candidate: A COMPULSORY ON-SITE WRITTEN EXAM. Quote: 'Written exam (3 hours)' comprising 'task elaboration in interactive computer music/multimedia, text summarization and commentary, and multiple-choice questions on computer music and digital media terminology', followed by a '15-minute' oral in which the candidate must 'present three works of yours' (~10 min presentation + 5 min Q&A). Preparation explicitly expected in 'electronic music history, MAX/MSP software basics, and familiarity with key figures in electroacoustic composition'. 'The exam and presentation are in English.' Held in person in Hamburg.
portfolioSpec: 'at least three representative works' demonstrating artistic use of digital media, especially computer music; at the oral he presents 'excerpts of these pieces' within ~10 minutes. No file format or per-work duration published — UNVERIFIED on that detail.
costForTunisian: No tuition fee (state Hochschule in Hamburg); a semester contribution applies. The exact amount is not published on the pages reached — UNVERIFIED. An application fee is referenced on the application page but the amount is likewise not shown — UNVERIFIED.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE: for applicants whose degree is from a non-EU country the deadline reported is 1 April for the winter semester (10 January for summer); entrance examination 27–28 April 2026. NOTE: the 1 April date comes from a third-party aggregator, not from an HfMT page I could open — treat as INDICATIVE, not verified.
languageOfInstruction: English, and — importantly — EXEMPT from the German B2 rule. Quote from HfMT's German-knowledge page: 'In the Contemporary Performance and Composition (CoPeCo)/Master's and Multimedia Composition/Master's degree programs, teaching takes place in English.' The general rule it overrides is 'proof of a good knowledge of German at level B2'. No specific English certificate score is published — UNVERIFIED.
correction: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The gate is not a soft 'portfolio + interview': it is a THREE-HOUR ON-SITE WRITTEN EXAMINATION in computer-music theory, Max/MSP and electroacoustic history, plus an oral presentation — he must travel to Hamburg and sit a knowledge test. (2) Positively: HfMT's blanket German B2 admission requirement does NOT apply to this programme, which is explicitly named as English-taught.
verdictWhy: The three-hour written examination on computer-music terminology, Max/MSP and the electroacoustic canon is exactly the thing a self-taught producer with a software degree and no conservatoire background cannot bluff, and it is sat in person in Hamburg at his own expense. The German exemption and zero tuition are genuinely attractive, but they do not change the fact that he would be examined on a syllabus he has never studied. Revisit only if he spends a year seriously studying computer-music history and Max/MSP.

institution: Technische Universität Berlin together with Royal Conservatoire The Hague
programme: Audio Communication and Sonology (joint double-degree master)
stillExists2027: YES the arrangement exists — but IT IS NOT A PROGRAMME YOU CAN APPLY TO. It is an internal exchange track, capped: the Royal Conservatoire 'agreed to accept as a host university each year up to 6 students'.
award: Two degrees at the end: 'a Master of Science from the TU Berlin and a Master of Music in Sonology from the Royal Conservatoire'. Both real second-cycle degrees — but only reachable after first being admitted to, and completing a year of, TU Berlin's German-taught M.Sc.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO — not as an entry route
acceptsQuote: DECISIVE: 'The programme is open to TU Berlin students enrolled in the Audio Communication and Technology master programme who successfully completed the mandatory modules up to 39 ECTS.' And from the Sonology side: 'Candidates apply for the master's programme Audio Communication and Technology at the TU Berlin first; until 15 February of the following year they can apply for a change to The Hague.' The real entry gate is therefore the TU Berlin M.Sc., whose own requirement is 'a first university degree in a science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law programme' PLUS 'knowledge of higher mathematics (minimum 10 credit points)' and programming — a software engineer passes the academic test easily.
liveAudition: No audition anywhere in the process. Selection for the exchange is 'based on their academic, artistic, personal and linguistic qualifications' plus 'a research project proposal'. The blocker is language and sequencing, not performance.
portfolioSpec: NO PORTFOLIO IS REQUIRED for the exchange — what is required is 'a research project proposal'. The input's 'Portfolio only' label is wrong.
costForTunisian: TU Berlin charges no tuition, only a compulsory semester fee for social contribution and transport (amount not published on the pages reached — UNVERIFIED). At the Royal Conservatoire 'all students...must pay the regular tuition fees per academic year' — the Dutch non-EEA institutional rate, which is substantial and was not published on the linked page (UNVERIFIED amount). Travel, accommodation, books and equipment are the student's own.
funding: UNVERIFIED — none advertised for the exchange itself.
applicationDeadline: 'The deadline for application to the exchange is 15 February for the current year' — but that is the deadline for someone ALREADY at TU Berlin. The deadline that matters to him is the TU Berlin M.Sc. admission deadline, which was not published on the pages reached (UNVERIFIED).
languageOfInstruction: DECISIVE PROBLEM. 'The main language of instruction in the Master's programme is German' (TU Berlin M.Sc.), with 'German: C1 level required for international applicants' and English B2. The exchange itself additionally requires 'Proficiency in English at least on a level equivalent to the evaluation scales IELTS (6,0) or TOEFL (ibT level 83)' and 'Proficiency in German at least on level TDN 4 / TestDaF'.
correction: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE INPUT MISREPRESENTS THIS ENTIRELY. (1) It is not a master's programme one applies to; it is a capped internal exchange (max 6 students/year) available only to students already enrolled at TU Berlin who have completed 39 ECTS. (2) The gate is not 'Portfolio only' — there is no portfolio at all, only a research project proposal. (3) It is not language-neutral: the host M.Sc. is taught in German and demands German C1 for international applicants, with TestDaF TDN 4 for the exchange. A candidate with no German cannot enter.
verdictWhy: He cannot apply to this at all — it is an internal exchange for people already a year into TU Berlin's Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc., which is taught in German and requires German C1 from international applicants. With zero German he is not merely uncompetitive, he is ineligible for the only entry door. Delete it from the list and spend the time on the Erasmus Mundus application instead.

programme: Music (MA) — Sonic Arts / Sound Engineering & Design concentration
stillExists2027: YES — MIAM's thesis MA runs nine concentration areas including 'Sound Engineering and Design, Sonic Arts'. ITU publishes an annual international graduate admission cycle; the most recent published one is 2026-2027 Fall.
award: A real thesis master's degree from a state technical university — ITU awards a 'Music Masters' diploma via the Graduate School. Second cycle, not a certificate.
acceptsQuote: DECISIVE AND UNUSUALLY OPEN: 'There are no department / concentration area requirements' and 'ALES/GMAT/GRE' are not required for this route. A software-engineering BSc is admissible on its face; for Sound Engineering and Design it is arguably an advantage.
liveAudition: NO AUDITION FOUND on MIAM's own pages. Selection is portfolio + documents + an INTERVIEW: ITU's international graduate calendar schedules 'Interviews: July 01 - 03, 2026'. MIAM's Turkish-language announcements refer to a 'giriş sınavı' (entrance examination) whose detailed content sits in a downloadable application guide I could not open — so the exact interview/exam content is UNVERIFIED. For performance concentrations an audition would exist; for Sonic Arts / SED the published requirement is a portfolio.
portfolioSpec: 'Candidates must prepare a portfolio relevant to their application area' — no number of works, no duration, no format published on the English page. UNVERIFIED in detail; the detail lives in the 'MIAM Başvuru Kılavuzu' PDF which did not render. Also required: 'Two letters of recommendations must be submitted by the candidate', transcripts, statement of purpose, CV.
costForTunisian: UNVERIFIED. Neither the MIAM programme page nor the ITU international graduate announcement I opened publishes the international-student tuition figure. ITU is a state university and international graduate tuition is set annually by the council; I will not assert a number. What IS verified: no application-stage ALES/GRE/GMAT fee burden, and no English certificate cost at master's level.
funding: UNVERIFIED at the level of amount and deadline. The input claims 'Full' funding; nothing on the pages I reached substantiates a MIAM or ITU scholarship with a stated amount. The realistic route is the Türkiye Bursları national scholarship, which is a SEPARATE and much earlier application (typically opening January–February) — not automatic on admission.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026-2027 Fall, international applicants): 'April 24, 2026 09:00 - June 26, 2026 17:00 (UTC/GMT+3)', interviews 'July 01 - 03, 2026', results 'July 08, 2026', registration 'July 09, 2026 09:00 - July 14, 2026 17:00'. Expect the same late-April-to-late-June window for the 2027-2028 cycle.
languageOfInstruction: English. Quote: 'The educational language of the program is %100 English.' And crucially for him: 'English certificate is not mandatory in the Master applications' (ITU international graduate announcement) — no IELTS needed at master's level, unlike PhD.
correction: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) 'Funding: Full' is NOT SUBSTANTIATED by any ITU/MIAM page — there is no automatic full scholarship on admission; the only credible full-funding route is Türkiye Bursları, a separate national competition with its own earlier deadline. (2) Positively, the input's 'Portfolio only' understates it slightly — there IS an interview stage (1–3 July in the prior cycle), though not an audition.
verdictWhy: The admissions logic is the friendliest he will find anywhere: 'There are no department / concentration area requirements', no GRE, no IELTS at master's level, English-taught, and a June deadline that fits a September 2027 start. The condition is money — the 'Full funding' in his list is unverified and almost certainly means Türkiye Bursları, a separate national competition he must apply to months earlier and may not win, with the international tuition figure unpublished. Apply, but resolve the funding question in writing with MIAM before counting on it.
